Executive Order 11040
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTE
BETWEEN THE BELT RAILWAY COMPANY OF CHICAGO AND
CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS a dispute exists between The Belt Railway Company 
of Chicago, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by 
the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organization; and
W HEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
this dispute within thirty days from the date of-this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by The 
Belt Railway Company of Chicago, or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which this dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11040 (signed 1962-08-06, 27 FR 7857), read in full from the held official FR text layer (27 FR 7857, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11040.txt offsets 543-2026; the representation is the official FR page OCR, location_verified false, page check not required by the record). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The order creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between The Belt Railway Company of Chicago and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers ('I hereby create a board of three members', offset 1355 onward), directs it to report 'within thirty days from the date of-this order' (offset 1590 onward) and recites the section 10 status quo (offset 1866 onward). Deciding source: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt), whose operative sentence (offsets 691-966) revokes 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto', and whose table names this order ('11040 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute', offsets 18012-18085); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1986-02-25. The end cites the dossier's ACT record (agent-located Rastell record, independently AI-reviewed, effective_class on_signing). Report-deadline ruling (2026-10-21, option C) applied: the report deadline (1962-09-05 (signing date 1962-08-06 plus 30 days; counting convention not ruled)) and the report itself are spent facts, not ends. Spent facts disclosed under the report-deadline ruling (not ends): the held NMB copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11040_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_11040_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ed6de90c70.txt, https://nmb.gov/NMB_Application/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/PEB-150-Report.pdf, sha256 002c3eea...) is dated on its cover 'March 4, 1963' (offset 1112) and its letter of transmittal says the board 'has been able to bring about a voluntary negotiated settlement of the dispute by the parties'; the order is functionally spent on 1963-03-04 (report) and the section 10 status quo ran 30 days after the report (about 1963-04-03). Two discrepancies for the reviewer: the cover reads 'APPOINTED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER 11041' while the transmittal letter names 'Executive Order No. 11040' and the same date and parties, and the report date falls after the 30-day deadline with no held extension instrument. The transmittal letter's own day is OCR-garbled ('Ma~'ch /~, 1963'). The report text is not dossier evidence, so it is disclosed here rather than attached as a later_event; existing FETCH_QUEUE line 407 already requests this report-date source. D6 / later events: the dossier chain and actor provisions show only EO 12553; the draft's later-event and whole-order-end proposals (OFR disposition note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986' and the 1989 Codification table 'Revoked by EO 12553') point to the same instrument and are attached as the end itself; a by-number scan of all held FR order texts and APP texts found no other naming instrument (EO_9289, EO_9602 and EO_12593 (FR page numbers 11040 in contents lists), EO_12553 (the revocation)). Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR or text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. No conflicts are listed in the draft or dossier. Machine searches pasted after review: OFR catalog (1937 onward; covers this order), U.S. Code and eCFR (0 hits for this order: no current-law citation). Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15): heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966, the 'No. Subject' table and the signature block were read; a word search of the whole held text for saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that and effective finds no savings, exception, pending-matter or transfer wording (the only 'effective' hit, line 597, is the subject column of another row). Own-residual check, reading EO 11040 in full (27 FR 7857, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11040.txt offsets 543-2026): it created an ad hoc fact-finding board for one labor dispute and set its report duty; it created no office, fund, property or private right that could outlast the board, and any status-quo obligation was the statute's own and long spent. EO 12553 has no savings clause, and nothing of the order outlives its revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts in jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts (every hit read in context: EO_9289, EO_9602 and EO_12593 (FR page numbers 11040 in contents lists), EO_12553 (the revocation)); a by-number scan of the held American Presidency Project order texts (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts: no other order names it); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986): 'it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' (held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, offsets 691-966), followed by the table entry '11040 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute' (offsets 18012-18085). EO 12553 states no effective date (no 'effective', 'take effect', savings or exception wording in the held text), so the revocation took effect on signing, 1986-02-25.

whole_order_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986): 'it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' (held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, offsets 691-966), followed by the table entry '11040 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute' (offsets 18012-18085).
